prepay.basis: Customer deposits of $143.9m at 30 Jun 2026 (10-Q) against the ESDS and global-technology contracts — cash security held in escrow, released on acceptance (8-K 20 Aug 2026) and, for the first cluster, applied to repay Facility A of the GPU-backed loan (8-K 1 Oct 2026); carried as the opening prepayment balance, credited over twenty quarters. NVIDIA pays no prepayment: the block’s ~$3.75bn of hardware is excluded from the prepayment base in the quarters it is paid (special.replaceG). Future contracts: prepayment at execution “allows Sharon AI to submit the purchase order” (Q2 deck) — modelled at 15% of GPU capex on contracted capacity, credited evenly over the five-year term (SemiAnalysis: “credited equally throughout contract life”). Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry. Explicit opening-balance credits retain their own dated schedules. Mixed future tranches allocate inferred credits by contractual IT MW; purchase capex remains scheduled if delivery slips.

finance.wfMarginBasis: the quarterly waterfall runs at 60% EBITDA: the company guides to ~75% gross margin, SemiAnalysis’s contract-level margins after colocation ($100/kW-month) and power ($0.05/kWh) are 88–91%, and Bloomberg consensus carries ~50% in 2027 once corporate costs and the NVIDIA revenue share are charged; 60% sits between the tenant peers (CoreWeave 57–59%) and the company’s guide
finance.basis: debt 9.95% (the US$356m senior secured GPU-backed SPV facility of 28 Sep 2026, fixed, excluding fees; Facility A $150m repaid from the escrowed customer deposit on acceptance, Facility B $206m a bullet term loan), 20%/yr pool amortisation (GPU facilities sized to the five-year contracts), $150m cash floor; lenders advance 80% of GPU cost on contracted capacity (SemiAnalysis sizes up to 80% LTC at 1.3× DSCR), 50% on spot; no shell capex — every site is leased colocation (NEXTDC, GreenSquareDC, a New Zealand provider), rent inside EBITDA, the ~$623m NEXTDC 72 MW commitment and the GreenSquareDC 120-month term are service contracts, not debt; 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $27 (the 19 Oct 2026 mark) plus the residual the flywheel cannot cover; the two convertible series (6.00% due May 2031 $350m at $48.24, 4.75% due Jun 2032 $700m at $99.66, no capped calls, carried at fair value $1.007bn in the 10-Q, principal $1.05bn used here) convert only if the model’s 2030 price clears the strike; certificates of deposit $12.7m counted; fully diluted before converts 43.32m = 35.667m Class A + 0.136m Class B (160 votes a share, one economic share) + 6.375m pre-funded warrants at $0.0001 + 1.139m options and RSUs (10-Q anti-dilutive list); the 22.25m SPAC warrants (SHAZW) are exercisable for only 444,982 shares in aggregate and are ignored; the 1.2m-share plan increase and annual evergreen (28 Aug 2026) are not counted

notes: 212 MW secured, 120 MW contracted. Every megawatt is leased colocation: NEXTDC Melbourne and Sydney (up to 87 MW, including the 72 MW NVIDIA site), GreenSquareDC (15 MW, 120-month term from a September 2026 ready-for-service date), a New Zealand provider (14 MW) and 80 MW added on 20 August with no site named.Q2-26 10-Q · 8-K 20 Aug

The NVIDIA site lands in 2027. The amended and restated NEXTDC service order for 72 MW deploys in five phases from April to August 2027 and commits ~$623m over its term; the company is “substantially dependent on NEXTDC”.10-Q commitments note and risk factors

Beyond 212 MW is not modelled. Management speaks of a “gigawatt-scale” ambition across Australia, New Zealand and Asia-Pacific; the page stops at the secured footprint, and the signed-book-only scenario stops at 120 MW.8-K 1 Oct 2026

64,600 GPUs by 2027Q3 on the contracted book — 40,000 GB300 for NVIDIA, 8,208 B300 for ESDS, ~7,000 in New Zealand, ~4,752 for the global technology company, 2,048 for the AI platform, ~2,500 merchant. The company says 68,000+ by mid-2027.8-Ks · 1 Oct release · SemiAnalysis counts

Five-year book life. SemiAnalysis models a five-year depreciation schedule; consensus D&A implies the same. The refresh reserve here is a house allowance, not the accounting life.SemiAnalysis · Bloomberg consensus

Density is the company’s own. 40,000 GB300 on 72 MW is 556 per MW (~1.8 kW all-in); the ESDS cluster 547 per MW. The house 400 per MW used on the other pages would put ~30% more megawatts behind the same GPUs.8-K 12 Jun · 8-K 1 Apr

Contract cohorts. The signed book keeps its filed all-in rate until expiry: ESDS $3.48, the AI platform $4.16, New Zealand $4.31, the global technology company $4.56 per GPU-hour — $16.7–19.0m per IT MW-year, the top of the GB300 ladder. New capacity uses the shared house curve.

The NVIDIA block is a floor, not a price. Up to $4.88bn over six years on 40,000 GPUs is $2.32 per GPU-hour on average; capacity reserved for NVIDIA can be sold to third parties with NVIDIA taking an undisclosed share above the floor. The page carries $3.29 (owner ruling, 3 Aug 2026); the floor and a 40%-share placement are scenarios.8-K 12 Jun 2026 · SemiAnalysis

Evidence. Contract dollars and terms are filed; GPU counts on two contracts are inferred; no customer is named except ESDS and NVIDIA. The ESDS counterparty was challenged in a 30 April short report that filings do not rebut.

Prepay, then borrow against the contract. Customer prepayment at execution funds the purchase order; the inaugural $356m GPU-backed SPV facility (9.95% fixed, 28 Sep 2026) is “the first in an expected series”, with Facility A repaid from the escrowed customer deposit on acceptance.Q2 deck · 8-K 1 Oct 2026

$2.6bn raised in ten months. $125m IPO (Feb), $100m pre-IPO notes (converted at $12.53), $350m 6.00% converts (May), $900m of equity and pre-funded warrants at $68.73 plus $700m 4.75% converts (June), $74m from the TCDC sale, $356m of GPU debt (Sep).10-Q · 8-Ks

The catch: the NVIDIA block alone needs ~$4bn of hardware against $1.86bn of cash. At today’s price the residual equity in the model is raised at $27, against a June placement at $68.73; the converts (strikes $48.24 and $99.66) stay debt unless the price recovers.funding stack · summary table

Costs are rent and power. SemiAnalysis’s inputs — colocation $100 per kW-month, power $0.05/kWh — leave 88–91% contract-level margins; the company guides ~75% gross; consensus carries ~50% EBITDA in 2027 once overhead and the NVIDIA share are charged. The page runs 60%.SemiAnalysis · Bloomberg

Capex is $42m per MW on the customer clusters and ~$56m on the NVIDIA block ($4bn committed for 72 MW, including networking, storage and the VAST layer). No shell: the landlord’s capital sits in the rent.10-Q · SemiAnalysis per-deal capex

Maintenance, not replacement. Tray swap at 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares — the same house allowance as the other pages — on a five-year take-or-pay book that fully recovers the hardware inside the term.model

Some equity, not none. Base: 10% of the 2027–28 build plus whatever the prepayments, the GPU facilities and operating cash cannot cover, issued at $27 — the bridge shows the count. The June placement was at $68.73; the price has since fallen by more than half.8-K 17 Jun 2026 · Finnhub

The NVIDIA economics are the swing. Floor versus placement moves the 72 MW block between $2.32 and $3.49 per GPU-hour; every $1 per GPU-hour on the block is ~$175m a year retained. The signed-book-only scenario shows what the 120 MW contracted today is worth on its own.scenarios · SemiAnalysis
EPS is the long-run anchor. Pick your multiple.after the raise

footer.model: Shared pricing and contract-cohort model (spec §6i). Existing commitments, estimated coverage, same-hardware renewals and new business are distinguished. Pricing, expiry and continuity assumptions are exposed with their evidence. Company financing and capex retain the dated research snapshot.

capexBasis: by energisation quarter, $m: the NVIDIA block at the filed ~$4bn hardware commitment (10-Q: “committed to procure additional high-performance computing hardware and related infrastructure for approximately $4 billion” = ~$56m per IT MW incl. networking, storage and the VAST data layer), less the $256m of deposits already paid to WWT Australia by 30 June, paid ahead of the Apr–Aug 2027 phases; the B300/GB300 customer clusters at $42m per IT MW (SemiAnalysis per-deal capex $39–44m per MW, $75–83k per GPU); the uncontracted 92 MW at $45m per MW (Rubin-era); no shell capex — every data centre is leased colocation

market.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
market.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
market.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

market.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.
